Unconstrained subgroup optimization

Source: R/group_optimize_unconstrained.R
group_optimize_unconstrained.Rd

Refine sampled subgroup levels so that the subgroup statistics observed in the data match the published subgroup statistics in summary. Patient counts are not preserved.

Usage

group_optimize_unconstrained(
  patient,
  summary,
  iterations = 1000L,
  tolerance = 1e-06
)

Arguments

patient

Patient-level survival data, the output of group_data_patient().

summary

Summary subgroup statistics, the output of group_data_summary().

iterations

Non-negative whole number, the maximum number of iterations for each subgroup variable. Each iteration draws one patient and fits one Cox model per subgroup level.

tolerance

Non-negative number. The search for each subgroup variable stops when the loss \(\Delta(x)\) falls below tolerance. The loss is a sum of squares, so the default of 1e-6 stops when the observed and published statistics agree to roughly 1e-3.

Value

A tibble with the same rows and columns as patient, in the same order. Each subgroup column is a factor of the optimized levels whose levels are those of the subgroup variable in summary$level, in the same order. All other columns are unchanged.

Details

group_optimize_unconstrained() implements the "Optimization for unconstrained sampling" section of vignette("optimization", package = "retrogroup"), separately for each subgroup variable. The loss \(\Delta(x)\) is the squared Euclidean distance between the observed and published log hazard ratios, plus the squared distance between the observed and published standard errors for the subgroup levels whose standard_error in summary is not NA. The observed statistics come from a Cox proportional hazards model of each subgroup level with treatment as the only covariate, as in survival::coxph(). If the model cannot be fit for some subgroup level, for example because the level is empty or one of its arms has no events, the loss is infinite.

Each iteration draws a patient \(i\) uniformly at random and moves that patient to the subgroup level \(k\) that minimizes \(\Delta(x^{(i \to k)})\). The patient stays put if the current level ties for the minimum, so the loss never increases. The search for each subgroup variable stops when the loss falls below tolerance or after iterations iterations, whichever comes first. If the loss of any subgroup variable is still at least tolerance after iterations iterations, group_optimize_unconstrained() throws a warning of class "retrogroup_warning" that lists those subgroup variables and their final losses.

The search is greedy, so it may settle in a local minimum. The number of patients in each subgroup level is not guaranteed to equal the published number of patients in summary. Use group_optimize_constrained() on the output of group_sample_constrained() to preserve the published counts.

In addition to the requirements of group_analysis_probability(), patient must have one column per subgroup variable in summary, named after the subgroup variable, with no missing values and only the levels of that subgroup variable in summary. The output of group_sample_unconstrained() satisfies these requirements. These columns are the starting subgroup levels, and all other columns of patient are returned unchanged.

Optimization uses R's random number generator. Call set.seed() beforehand for reproducible results.

See also

Other optimization: group_optimize_constrained()

Examples

  patient <- group_data_patient(
    group_example_patient(),
    arm = "arm",
    treatment = "Lev+5FU",
    time = "time",
    event = "event"
  )
  summary <- group_data_summary(
    group_example_summary(),
    variable = "variable",
    level = "level",
    patients = "patients",
    log_hazard_ratio = "log_hazard_ratio",
    standard_error = "standard_error"
  )
  summary <- summary[summary$variable == "age", ]
  set.seed(0)
  sample <- group_sample_unconstrained(patient, summary)
  optimized <- group_optimize_unconstrained(
    sample,
    summary,
    tolerance = 1e-4,
    iterations = 100L
  )
  summary
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   variable level      patients log_hazard_ratio standard_error
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <int>            <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 age      under 60        280           -0.169          0.178
#> 2 age      60 or over      339           -0.546          0.160
  group_analysis_summary(sample, "age")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   variable level      patients log_hazard_ratio standard_error
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <int>            <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 age      under 60        276           -0.175          0.175
#> 2 age      60 or over      343           -0.533          0.162
  group_analysis_summary(optimized, "age")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   variable level      patients log_hazard_ratio standard_error
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <int>            <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 age      under 60        277           -0.164          0.175
#> 2 age      60 or over      342           -0.542          0.162
